title: Common-stage composition descends to directed Hom quotients
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set, $O$ a set of labels and $r:O\to I$. For $a,b\in O$ and $k\ge r(a),r(b)$ give sets $H_k(a,b)$ and transition maps $t^{ab}_{kn}:H_k(a,b)\to H_n(a,b)$ for $k\le n$, with $t_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $t_{np}t_{kn}=t_{kp}$. Give products $\mu_k:H_k(b,c)\times H_k(a,b)\to H_k(a,c)$ whenever $k\ge r(a),r(b),r(c)$ and elements $e_{a,k}\in H_k(a,a)$ for $k\ge r(a)$. Assume the products are associative and unital at each stage, and
$$t^{ac}_{kn}(\mu_k(h,g))=\mu_n(t^{bc}_{kn}h,t^{ab}_{kn}g),\qquad t^{aa}_{kn}(e_{a,k})=e_{a,n}.$$
Let $Q(a,b)$ be the quotient of $\coprod_{k\ge r(a),r(b)}H_k(a,b)$ by the equivalence relation generated by $(k,g)\sim(n,t_{kn}g)$; write $[k,g]$ for its classes. Thus it is the set colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the given Hom diagram.
For representatives $f=(k,g)$ and $f'=(l,h)$ define $B_m(f,f')=[m,\mu_m(t_{lm}h,t_{km}g)]$ for $m\ge k,l$. Then $B_m(f,f')=B_n(f,f')$ for any two such upper bounds $m,n$. If one input is replaced by a generating-related representative, $B$ is unchanged, separately in each input. Hence there is a unique binary operation on the quotient sets satisfying
$$[l,h]\circ[k,g]=[m,\mu_m(t_{lm}h,t_{km}g)].$$
For any three composable representatives and any common upper stage $p$ of their stages, both bracketings are the classes at $p$ of the corresponding bracketings of their transported stage arrows. The elements $[r(a),e_{a,r(a)}]$ are two-sided identities. Consequently these operations give a category on $O$ with Hom sets $Q(a,b)$. This assertion includes independence of the chosen upper bound, descent in both quotient variables, the same-stage product formula, associativity, and both unit laws; it does not assume a category on the representative sets.
